residual_risk: Behaviour change for new adopters only: a fresh board no longer carries claude-track / claude-p / claude-action / copilot-cli / codex. Anyone who wants one adds it with `hkb init --profiles <name>` (additive) — the tick's skip message now says so. Existing boards, including this repo's, are unaffected.
A board.json that exists but has no `profiles` key still loads as all six via loadBoard (src/board.js:186) — unchanged, and init over it stays additive.
No smoke run: nothing in `files` or in what the CLI reads from the package at runtime changed.
verification: npm run lint && npm test — 430 pass, 0 fail (3 new boardProfiles cases in test/harness.test.js)

end-to-end: real `hkb init` in scratch git repos against a fake `gh` — bare init = [claude] + 11 labels; --profiles claude,codex = [claude,codex] + 12; --with-actions = [claude,claude-action]; a second init --harness codex over a board with a hand-added `homegrown` profile and max_in_progress:7 kept both and added codex

results.summary: A fresh `hkb init` now seeds board.json with exactly the profiles that were resolved (`--profiles` / `--harness` / `--with-actions`), instead of all six DEFAULT_PROFILES: a bare init yields `claude` and 11 kb:* labels, `--profiles claude,codex` yields two and 12. Re-running init over an existing board stays additive — a profile the operator added or tuned by hand is never touched. The logic is a new pure `boardProfiles(existing, profiles, onUnknown)` in src/init.js, beside `resolveProfiles`, mirroring loadBoard's "keep only what the user declared". Fallout handled in the same change: the tick's `unknown profile <name>` skip now names the fix (`hkb init --profiles <name>`), because claude-track/claude-p are no longer on every board by default; docs/harnesses.md gained a "Which profiles a board gets" section, the README a paragraph, and the CLI help now reads `--profiles a,b`. Draft PR: https://github.com/emyann/harness-kanban-board/pull/75
